answer: Forced Entry-Point Divergence. Each agent must route first registration through a distinct, randomly assigned entry haven from a large pool; the pool records which entry point each identity used. Enforcement: two identities sharing every recorded entry point are flagged as clones and lose access until one diverges. A clone controller must split traffic across separate entry knolls, paying per-entry routing and separate handshakes. Cloning a thousand agents now demands a thousand distinct entry paths, raising attacker cost to near the coordination zenith for each copy.
